text:
Maria (PM): Quick sync on prompt-sets / evals UI. I prototyped a compact diff list + inline scorecard legend. Main asks: how do we make keyboard bulk-select discoverable, what copy goes into the bulk-approve confirmation, and can we avoid the large modal for single-item approves?

Ben (Designer): Uploaded new Figma frame. Idea: add a small persistent left rail for filters, and a compact mode toggle that collapses metadata. Diffs render in a dense list with chevron to expand full output.

deploy-bot: New design file uploaded by Ben: https://redwood.design/figma/xyz123 :white_check_mark:

Zoe (ENG): Compact mode ok. Implementation note: virtualized window + variable row height once expanded. We should preserve scroll position when toggling compact. Also recommend storing user density preference server-side.

Lucas (Frontend): Keyboard flow: Use Space/Enter to toggle expand, Shift+Arrow to select range, and `a` to toggle all on page. Need visible focus styles. For single-item approve, use an inline confirm (small dropdown) rather than a full-screen modal.

Priya (A11y): A11y checklist: 1) Ensure selection region is announced with `aria-live` when range selected. 2) Inline confirm must be keyboard-accessible and trap focus only if it opens a modal. 3) Approve buttons should include context: say "Approve evaluation 12345" for screen readers. 4) Color tokens for score bands need >=4.5:1 contrast.

Nadia (ProdEng): Analytics: need events `compact_mode_toggled`, `select_range_start`, `select_range_end`, `inline_approve_shown`, `bulk_approve_executed`. Include run_id, user_id, selection_count. Also, bulk_approve API should return an `undo_window_ms` and an `undo_token` if we want client-side undo.

Maria (PM): Copy for bulk modal draft: "Approve 12 evaluations — these will be marked as accepted for Run #5472. This action can be undone within 5 minutes." Is that too wordy?

Ben (Designer): Slight tweak: "Approve 12 evaluations — marked accepted for Run #5472. You can undo this action for 5 minutes." Shorter and keeps the verb.

Priya (A11y): Add a link to docs in the modal copy: "Learn how undo works" with `rel=noopener` and clear focus target.

Zoe (ENG): Backend considerations: bulk approve should be idempotent. Undo should queue a reverse job; keep messages in a Kafka topic so we can replay in case of partial shard failures. We'll surface an `optimistic_state_id` so front-end can reconcile.

Lucas (Frontend): UI sketch: when user invokes Shift+Arrow, show a small overlay saying "Selecting 3 items — press Enter to confirm" with clear keyboard affordances. Will prototype animation and focus handling.

Maria (PM): Decision checklist for Monday: 1) Add compact mode toggle (persisted), 2) Inline single-approve confirm, 3) Range-select keyboard (Shift+Arrow) + `a` for select all, 4) Bulk approve modal copy uses Ben's short variant + undo link, 5) A11y fixes per Priya, 6) Analytics events to Nadia, 7) Backend undo/idempotency notes to Zoe.

Ben (Designer): I'll update Figma to include the inline confirm pattern and a visible small help hint for keyboard selection.

Zoe (ENG): I'll open infra ticket for kafka topic + bulk-approve idempotency. ETA: next sprint.

Lucas (Frontend): I'll wire keyboard handlers and the select overlay in a feature branch. Will include unit tests for focus management.

Priya (A11y): I'll draft the screen-reader script and run through NVDA and VoiceOver checks. Posting checklist on the PR.

Nadia (ProdEng): I'll add analytics schema and example payloads to the tracking PR.

Maria (PM): Nice. One UI nit from support: users confuse "Filter evaluations" with workspace search. Ben, can we use placeholder "Filter by prompt text, tag, or eval id" and an inline tooltip explaining scope?

Ben (Designer): Yep. Adding placeholder and tooltip. Tooltip will be keyboard-focusable.

deploy-bot: Reminder: design review sync Monday 10:00am in #design-reviews calendar invite.

Maria (PM): Great thread. If no objections, moving decisions to the design ticket and assigning owners. :rocket:

Zoe (ENG): No objections.

Priya (A11y): I'll review the updated prototype before final sign-off.

Lucas (Frontend): Thumbs up.

Ben (Designer): Updated Figma link: https://redwood.design/figma/xyz123?version=2
